extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), commanders, and other Army staff responsible for public affairs, media, and community engagement
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedural standards governing Army public affairs activities, including exhibits, donations, support to organizations, funding, media travel, contracting, and use of military resources for PA purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits must conform to regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits displayed in designated Pentagon exhibit space must conform to this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General requirement: all Armed Forces exhibits at the Pentagon concourse and other designated areas must comply with the AR 360–1 provisions on exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: No classified material in exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: No classified material will be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit proposals that include classified information are disallowed; ensure all displayed content is unclassified prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit weight limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum permissible weight of an exhibit on the Pentagon concourse is 150 pounds per square foot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design exhibits to stay within the 150 lb/ft² floor-loading limit; consult facilities if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial content restriction for Pentagon exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals, projects, or products offered by commercial concerns may be construed as promotional; therefore only items currently in the military inventory or in a service-testing program may be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to a commercial concern is limited to a standard nameplate on military equipment or a 4-by-6-inch plaque crediting the lender placed in the lower right corner of an exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit request lead time and approval authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests are forwarded for display space to OCPA for ATSD (PA) approval at least 40 calendar days before the first day of the desired display period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit requests early (≥40 days) to allow OCPA and ATSD (PA) review; late requests may be disapproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data for Pentagon exhibit requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must contain: size of area desired, time desired, alternate dates, name/office/telephone of person in charge, special electrical requirements, title and brief description of the exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum space: 30 ft by 45 ft (three bays); normally maximum exhibit period is one week. If exhibit includes audio/visual, keep volume low to avoid interference with nearby commercial establishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security clearance documentation for exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that a proper security review has been made per paragraph 5–1 of this regulation. If the exhibit has not been cleared, four copies of text/diagrams/sketches/photographs and one copy of films/slides/sound tracks will accompany the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure security review is completed; if not cleared, submit required supporting materials with the space request to facilitate security vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial reference statement for exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that the display will contain no reference to a commercial concern other than a 4- by 6-inch plaque, credit line, or standard nameplate (on equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirm no promotional references beyond permitted small credit plaque; failure to do so may cause denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow AR references for lending/leasing materiel and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: General Army policy on lending or leasing materiel and facilities is in AR 700–131; other specific lending policies are in AR 725–1, AR 840–10, AR 840–1, AR 405–80, AR 735–5 as cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the cited ARs for detailed procedures and eligibility before lending or leasing Army materiel or facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explosives/pyrotechnics participation discouraged unless safety criteria met
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in rare cases, participation of Army personnel in public events involving use of explosives is not advisable because of injury and legal liability; units may approve participation when it meets established safety criteria, a risk assessment has been performed and accepted at the appropriate level per DA Pam 385–30, and participation is clearly in the interest of the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require a documented risk assessment per DA Pam 385–30 and high-level acceptance; default is to avoid Army involvement in explosive/pyrotechnic events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explosives on military installations discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: Using explosives in connection with events conducted on a military installation will be at the discretion of ACOMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACOMs must weigh safety and liability; follow local command policy for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antique weapons use prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Using antique weapons not routinely fired is prohibited, including using them for national salutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not authorize firing of antique weapons; consult AR 600–25 for routine salutes exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine salutes exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions do not apply to routine salutes as authorized in AR 600–25. Local commanders may approve rifle and cannon salutes conducted off-post as part of an approved PA program if a safety or risk assessment has been done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine, authorized salutes per AR 600–25 are allowed; ensure safety assessments for off-post salutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum exhibit policy reference
rubrics_metrics.description: AR 870–20 contains policy regarding Army museum exhibitry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult AR 870–20 for museum-specific exhibit policies, donations, and display standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized recipients for donation of obsolete/condemned combat equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 10 USC 2572, specified organizations (municipal corporations; Soldiers' Monument associations; state museums; incorporated educational museums; local posts/units of VFW/American Legion/recognized war veterans associations; recognized foreign war veterans associations; Sons of Veterans Reserve posts) are authorized to acquire such equipment for public display or ceremonial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify recipient eligibility against the statutory list and AR 870–20 before processing donations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility basis for recognizing veterans associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition for acquiring obsolete/condemned property is based upon the size and purpose of the organization and services rendered to veterans; organization must be composed of honorably discharged U.S. service members. Services rendered include informing veterans of employment rights and benefits and acting on behalf of disabled veterans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATSD (PA) evaluates eligibility considering organizational purpose, membership, and veteran services provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required for eligibility request to ATSD (PA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must contain a citation/copy of the charter granting recognition, a statement outlining the association's purpose and intended use of the property, names/titles/addresses of officers, copy of last financial statement, copy of constitution/charter/bylaws, total membership, and for local posts include written approval from national headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete documentation to ATSD (PA) to avoid delays; only after eligibility determination should requests for donations be sent to AMSTA-IM-OER.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA responsibilities for environmental protection
rubrics_metrics.description: PA responsibilities and support in connection with the Army Environmental Protection and Enhancement Program are in AR 200–1; PAOs must be familiar with environmental laws including NEPA and Executive Order 12088 and work closely with engineers and environmental coordinators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in two-way communication with environmental program managers; be aware that EIS processes may include public hearings of interest to media and public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land acquisition public engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform and engage the public about land acquisition studies throughout the acquisition process; Congressional notification must precede or coincide with public release; coordinate with local and ACOM PAOs and OCPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate early with legal and PA channels to ensure proper notification and messaging during land acquisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA activity rules during defense support of civil authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: During defense support of civil authorities operations, military PA activities, civil authority information support elements activities, public information actions, and news media access are subject to approval by the primary agency; the primary agency may establish a joint information center and DoD forces should coordinate with the joint field office per DoDD 3025.18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain primary agency approval and coordinate through established joint information structures when supporting civil authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCPA liaison with national service organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: OCPA maintains liaison with national service-oriented organizations; support to nongovernment organizations must conform to AR 1–50, DoD 5500.07–R and this regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the cited regulations when establishing or responding to liaison requests; ensure separation between Army interests and nongovernment organization business purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in meetings and cosponsorship limits
rubrics_metrics.description: DA personnel may participate as panel members, paper contributors, speakers, or spectators at meetings determined to be in the interest of the Army. Civic and community activities cosponsored by DA and industry or DA and nongovernment associations may be authorized if industry/association involvement is separate from their business purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review event purpose to ensure it aligns with Army interest and does not provide inappropriate commercial advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCPA notification for potentially high-interest cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: OCPA must be notified in advance of command cooperation in industry or nongovernment association programs that have the potential to generate significant public interest beyond the local or regional level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify OCPA early when an event or cooperation could attract national or wider attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hatch Act restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hatch Act restricts federal employee participation in partisan political activities during federal service; employees may not seek partisan public office, use official title when engaging in political activity, solicit or receive contributions for partisan candidates/groups, or engage in political activity while on duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs and others must avoid partisan political activities and consult ethics/legal counsel for borderline situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command membership rules for civic organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Command memberships in local civic organizations are authorized when deemed beneficial; only one command membership in each organization may be purchased for each ACOM and installation headquarters and should be registered in the name of the Army installation or command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer registration in the installation/command name to provide continuity; justify that membership supports morale, welfare, and mission objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding rules for memberships
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, command membership will be purchased with appropriated funds; commanders controlling nonappropriated welfare funds may approve Army-funded expenditures for command memberships only if membership supports morale/welfare/mission objectives and appropriated funds are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with funding source rules before purchasing memberships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on paying individual membership fees with appropriated funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Using appropriated funds to pay individual membership fees and dues in any society, club, or association is prohibited by 5 USC 5946, except for memberships in the name of and for the direct benefit of federal agencies when necessary to accomplish agency activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use appropriated funds for individual memberships; consult DoD 5500.07–R and DoDI 1000.15 for permitted agency memberships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting honorary offices with business-involved associations
rubrics_metrics.description: DA military and civilian personnel are prohibited from accepting an honorary office or membership in private associations whose membership includes business entities engaged in providing goods or services to a DoD component; an honorary office includes any position selection made on the basis of an official DA position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult local ethics counselor for questions about honorary positions or memberships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and documentation requirements for support to national military association conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Support must conform to 10 USC 2558, DoDD 5410.18, DoD 5500.07–R, AR 58–1 and this regulation. SECARMY has approval authority (delegable) to provide military support; ATSD (PA) retains authority to modify the list of approved national military associations. Requests to support unlisted associations must be submitted through Army channels to OCPA at least 90 days before the scheduled event and include statute copy, purpose statement, national officers, total membership, chapter locations, and constitution/charter/bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 90-day submission rule and provide complete documentation to be considered for DoD support and potential addition to DoD-designated lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on annual support to associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Army support to approved national military associations is limited to the annual conference or convention of each designated association (one conference/convention per calendar year); attendance and support must conform to current Army conference policy before obligating funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide recurring support for multiple events beyond the one annual conference without explicit authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for associations receiving support
rubrics_metrics.description: Military associations must be noncommercial, national in scope, and focus efforts on Regular Army, ARNG, or USAR activities. Associations primarily oriented toward a specific group of military veterans, a specific sex, military unit, campaign, ethnic group, religious group, or region are generally ineligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate associations against national scope and noncommercial tests; borderline cases require higher-level review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized logistical support conditions for association events
rubrics_metrics.description: While on duty, Army members are restricted to performing duties that relate directly to their military specialties. Use of personnel and equipment must be at no additional cost to the Government; logistical support must be incorporated into legitimate, scheduled training missions. Requests for general transportation reviewed by senior public affairs and legal officials prior to commander review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that support does not impose additional costs and is integrated into training where applicable; legal and senior PA review required for transportation support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air travel rules for association conference attendees
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference attendees who are military members traveling on official orders or traveling space available without orders may travel aboard military aircraft. Civilian spouses not designated by the military services cannot use military air transportation. Flights must be legitimately scheduled training missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit use of military air to authorized military attendees and scheduled training missions; civilian use is highly restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground transportation rules for association events
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Army-owned or -controlled nontactical vehicles is restricted to official purposes only; official conference attendees may travel via Government-owned or -contracted ground transportation; commanders determine whether event warrants general transportation and mass transportation is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mass transport for group movement; review requests per AR 58–1 and get legal/PA senior review when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical assistance support limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical support may be provided only for support of emergency and lifesaving functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide routine medical services for conferences unless they qualify as emergency/lifesaving support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting gratuities from contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting gratuities from private companies in connection with an association’s activities is prohibited. Except as specified in regulations, Army personnel are prohibited from attending social functions as guests of contractors, accepting hospitality, or accepting invitations unless sponsor demonstrates criteria (open seating, seating not selected/influenced by contractor interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult local ethics counselor on questionable hospitality; require sponsor assurances for event seating and guest list independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift acceptance limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepting gifts other than specialty advertising items of trivial intrinsic value for themselves or their families is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accept trivial advertising items; refuse gifts of substantive value and seek guidance if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry participation limited to appropriate event types
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, Army participation with industry will be limited to luncheons/dinners/meetings hosted by diverse business interests; public ceremonies of mutual interest (equipment demonstrations, first flights); industrial programs that support Government policy (industry seminars, international exhibits promoting U.S. achievements); civic/community-oriented projects where industry relationship is separate from business purpose; business-sponsored scouting; industry-subsidized awards; special events consistent with DoD 5500.07–R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure industry involvement is appropriate and separate from commercial promotion; avoid events that primarily benefit a single commercial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of unclassified material to industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Unclassified material and records for release outside DA will be made available upon request to industry representatives or associations representing the industry (see AR 25–55 and chap 7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AR 25–55 procedures for unclassified releases; withhold controlled/unreleased information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional community engagement support activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional support to nongovernment organizations can include designating DoD and Army coordinators, providing bands/troops/speakers, lending/leasing materiel, supporting major veterans conventions, and supporting community engagement activities governed by OCPA guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These supports are allowable when consistent with OCPA guidance and no inappropriate commercial benefit results.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA funding authority and consultation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: DFAS–IN Manual 37–100 provides fiscal authority on funding of PA equipment and activities. PA personnel should consult with the command or activity resource management office for clarification and guidance on funding issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with resource managers early in planning to ensure funding compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of organizational PA funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational PA funds may be used to defray costs of activities that are part of the command’s approved PA program, including civilian pay, travel, commercial printing, contracts/subscriptions/memberships, supplies, speaking engagements (requires legal review), support for civic events, public announcements of Army support to community events, equipment/software for PA/VI, PA training, and commercial internet media monitoring/transmission to digital platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure expenses are for approved PA program activities and get legal review where specified (e.g., speaking engagements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and no-additional-cost rule for event support
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Army resources to support public events will be at no additional cost to the Government; costs for Army participation in public events will be paid by event sponsors; costs the Army would have incurred notwithstanding support are not reimbursable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negotiate sponsor-funded arrangements for events that fall outside funded PA activities; distinguish reimbursable vs nonreimbursable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army will pay unprogrammed costs when in primary interest or authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army will pay all unprogrammed costs of supporting PA programs specifically authorized by public law, Executive order, Secretary of Defense, or SECARMY, and for official Federal Government functions, Army/civic observances of national holidays, official civil ceremonies/functions, and official speaking engagements when in primary interest of DA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm authorization basis before expending Army funds on unprogrammed PA activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events eligible for Army funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Events qualifying for Army funding include official Federal Government functions not political in nature; public observances of national holidays; public observance of Armed Forces Day/Week; national conventions of veterans associations; official civil ceremonies; speaking engagements; recruiting support including ROTC; appearances/demonstrations by special units; events of national/congressional/scientific/technical interest (with SecDef or unified commander approval); local events within PA outreach area; events recognizing military service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify event category against this list prior to requesting Army-funded support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for outside-funded events (10 USC 2012(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If event sponsors pay associated costs, official assistance must satisfy three criteria: (1) assistance accomplishes valid unit training requirements or involves tasks directly related to MOS; (2) assistance will not adversely affect training or ability to perform assigned functions; (3) event sponsors pay associated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how the assistance meets the three statutory criteria when entering sponsor-funded support agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor-paid additional costs list
rubrics_metrics.description: Event sponsors will pay additional costs ordinarily financed by the Army organization: travel/transportation of military personnel/equipment, meals/lodging/per diem, transportation/handling/aviation fuel not available at contract price, exhibit space/rental/utilities/custodial services, public liability/property damage insurance if required, other services per agreement, and possibly Army share via routine training transport.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear cost-reimbursement terms in agreements and require sponsors to cover specified categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on PA funds for hosting/representational entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: PA funds will not be expended for hosting and representational purposes such as luncheons, dinners, buffets, cocktail parties, theater tickets, gifts, and similar items or activities that would constitute entertainment events; such expenses may be charged only to SECARMY contingency fund for certain official receptions per AR 37–47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using PA funds for entertainment; route representational expenses through appropriate contingency funds when authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMA funds for incidental costs when sponsor agrees to pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Army operation and maintenance (OMA) funds may be used to pay incidental costs associated with unprogrammed community engagement activities when the event sponsor agrees to pay for the activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document sponsor agreement and ensure OMA funds usage complies with accounting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance principles and minimum necessary funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds programmed and expended for PA activities are part of each component’s OMA account and funding requirements will be kept to the minimum necessary to accomplish the Army’s objectives; beyond OMA funds, PA activities will be at no additional cost to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan PA budgets conservatively and justify expenditures against mission objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional items purchase criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Using PA funds to purchase and distribute promotional items for command-approved PA objectives is authorized within the limits of DoD 7000.14–R. Promotional items must clearly support the mission and PA objectives (examples: posters, pamphlets, information papers, booklets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure promotional items have clear PA purpose and comply with DoD financial rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting and reimbursement procedures references
rubrics_metrics.description: Financing will be accomplished according to DA Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution System (see AR 1–1). Procedures for reimbursement by other Government agencies are in DFAS–IN 37–1; reimbursement procedures for support to nongovernment programs are also in DFAS–IN 37–1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PPBE and DFAS procedures for budgeting and reimbursements; consult finance offices for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental hearing advertising funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Events and activities required by environmental laws, such as environmental hearings, will be paid with funds from the environmental program budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use environmental program funds for legally required notice/advertising; coordinate with environmental program managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA office contracting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PA office may contract with commercial firms for services and products; contracts will be awarded according to applicable laws, regulations, and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procurement laws and FAR requirements when contracting; coordinate with contracting officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting for Army-funded video/television production
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs may use the Production Acquisition Division (PAD) as a source for establishing multimedia and television production contracts; use of PAD helps ensure all applicable FAR required rights and data clauses are included so the Army owns all rights to productions and master materials and will not pay royalties or recurring license fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider PAD to centralize contracting and ensure rights ownership clauses are included to avoid recurring payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on using military transportation assets to compete with commercial carriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Military transportation assets will not be used to compete with commercial carriers of U.S. registry if commercial transportation is available, adequate, and meets PA objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commercial carriers when appropriate; military transportation is exceptional and must be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel/transportation must primarily serve DA/DoD interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel or transportation for PA purposes must be primarily in the interest of DA or DoD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how proposed travel advances Army/DoD interests; personal, goodwill-only trips are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: No commitment of military transportation until coordinated and approved
rubrics_metrics.description: No commitment of military transportation for PA purposes will be made until the request has been coordinated and approved by the command with primary interest; orders covering transportation will be issued by that command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow command coordination and order issuance procedures before making transportation commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD approval for travel arranged with other federal or foreign governments
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD must approve PA travel or transportation arranged with another federal agency or foreign government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain DoD-level approval for interagency or international transport arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanitarian/goodwill travel alone is not sufficient PA justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel to serve humanitarian purposes or increase goodwill does not, by itself, meet the criteria for PA travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure humanitarian/goodwill travel has an articulated PA interest or connects to training/mission requirements to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval authority for nonlocal community engagement travel by non-DoD persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval authority rests with SECARMY and is delegated to commanders in grade of major general (MG) or above and CNGB; may not be further delegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-DoD person travel on military carriers for community engagement requires high-level approval; plan for that approval cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander-authority for local travel approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Each commander with primary interest may grant approval for local travel or transportation for PA purposes if PA impact is confined primarily to the vicinity of that command, transportation is for an approved local PA program, and PA subject matter is not properly the responsibility of a higher command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local commanders can approve limited travel; use this authority only when criteria are clearly met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military transportation for media representatives space-available nonreimbursable
rubrics_metrics.description: Military transportation for media representatives, authors, and writers will be on a space available, nonreimbursable basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media travel via military transport is a courtesy on space-available basis and is not reimbursable; coordinate logistics and expectations with media outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local media travel approval and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Local travel is within the community outreach area; the commander in whose area the travel occurs may approve local travel for local news media representatives. News media representatives may be authorized travel when travel is an integral part of a story and is provided on a space available basis. All local travel for national/international media must be brought to OCPA's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define 'local' clearly and coordinate national/international media travel with OCPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonlocal media travel requires DoD approval and specific conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: All nonlocal media travel requires DoD approval. Nonlocal travel may be approved if travel is primarily in DoD interest, commercial transportation unavailable/inadequate, or travel available on space-available previously scheduled flights. Nonlocal travel may be approved when travel is integral to the story, coverage is major emergency and would be seriously impaired without transport, or the travel is of special interest as part of an approved PA project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OCPA Media Relations Division routing for nonlocal travel requests and justify based on the enumerated conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonlocal travel request content and POC responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for nonlocal travel must be forwarded through command channels to OCPA Media Relations Division and include dates, destinations, justification, and a point of contact who is familiar with regulations, will ensure proper briefings for security/travel requirements/gear, and will submit a news roll-up after the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete request packets and ensure the designated POC can perform all briefing and post-event reporting responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAOs not required to accompany media on nonlocal travel
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs are not required to accompany media representatives on nonlocal travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media can travel without PAO accompaniment if conditions and approvals are met, but PAOs must ensure media receive required briefings and security guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special travel category approvals (State adjutants, NGB, ARNG)
rubrics_metrics.description: State adjutants general approve PA travel within their states; NGB–PA office approves local travel to facilities outside their states or territories. Other media travel involving ARNG units requires DoD approval. Air transportation procedures for Members of Congress and staffs are in AR 1–20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the appropriate service-specific approval authorities for special categories of travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted and prohibited uses of Army aircraft for PA travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of qualifying PA activities for Army aircraft include authorized tours/conferences, joint tours with other agencies/foreign governments, authors/writers covering approved programs when travel is integral to the story (space available), and guests of SecDef/SECARMY for official programs. Approval may not be provided for record attempts, first flights of an aircraft entering inventory, first flight over isolated areas, or similar special flights. Army aviation assets are not used to transport persons costumed as holiday characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Army aircraft for publicity stunts, record attempts, or novelty flights; ensure passenger eligibility, mission purpose, and safety before approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orientation flight requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Orientation flights to support community engagement are to improve understanding of the Army mission; such flights may be provided only in suitable passenger-carrying aircraft, travelers must wear proper organizational uniforms if applicable and present proper identification, written parental consent required for passengers under 18, and flights will normally originate and terminate at the point of origin (exceptions case-by-case by commanders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow passenger eligibility, uniform/ID, consent, and routing rules; commanders may grant exceptions selectively.
